text:
Maria: heads-up — p99 for /v1/generate jumped ~120ms -> ~420ms at ~10:11 UTC, p50/p95 look stable though. dashboard endpoint breakdown shows weird divergence vs route-level p99.

Josh: hmm, we had a quota fallback at 10:11 for some clients, could be routing policy. Can you paste the console query you used?

Maria: sure, query I ran in console:
```
SELECT percentile(response_ms, [50,95,99])
FROM latency
WHERE endpoint='/v1/generate' AND timestamp >= '2024-05-05T10:05:00Z' AND timestamp <= '2024-05-05T10:20:00Z'
GROUP BY route, sample_source
```

Kevin: quick note — `sample_source` can be gateway, backend, cache_hit. Our rollup contract historically drops sample_source when computing route-level rollups, so the route p99 is computed from mixed-origin t-digests while endpoint p99 is recomputed from backend histograms after KV-cache filtering. That mismatch can explain different tails.

Maria: ugh that matches what I see: endpoint page shows backend-only p99 ~430ms, route view shows p99 ~180ms. How do we have a backend-only tail like that without showing on route?

Liz: Likely because gateway sampling favored short requests and cache hits (lots of low-latency samples) and only a few backend long requests were recorded in backend-only view. Route rollup pulls the high-volume gateway samples and masks the backend tail. We should annotate percentiles with sample origin. Suggestion: add a small badge like `p99 (gateway-sampled)` vs `p99 (backend-only)`.

Josh: @Liz can you spin up a quick UX PR? Minimal: show origin badge next to each percentile and hover to expose counts by origin + effective N. We need to prevent ops from chasing a false SLO when effective sample N is tiny.

incident-bot: quota-fallback triggered client=acme-corp at 2024-05-05T10:11:07Z — routing policy switched to fallback-model-v2 (lower-cost) for those keys.

Kevin: also remember last week's batching tweak — it batches short requests more aggressively which reduces gateway-observed tails. Long-seq requests end up unbatched and hit backend more, so tails shift. We should consider a sequence-length stratifier on the latency pane.

Maria: repro steps I ran locally:
1) issue POST /v1/generate with ~2000 tokens and header `x-client: dedicated-client`
2) observe backend p99 ~420ms for that window
logs: `req_id=... backend_ms=420 seq_len=2000 cache=false`

Liz: proposed tooltip copy: "Percentiles computed from sample origin X. Differences between endpoint and route views can be caused by sampling, KV-cache filtering, and route-level rollups. Hover to see per-origin counts and effective sample size (N)."

Josh: sounds good. Ops asks: Kevin, can you paste quick counts for 10:05-10:20 by sample_source so we can quantify?

Kevin: ran query, results:
```
window: 2024-05-05T10:05Z - 2024-05-05T10:20Z
gateway: 1,200
cache_hit: 1,020
backend: 80
```

Maria: that explains it — route rollup dominated by gateway/cache samples; backend has tiny N but contains the heavy tail. Proposal: add per-percentile effective-N and show a low-confidence indicator when N < 100.

Liz: +1 for effective-N and low-confidence warning. UX: red-outline or small `⚠ low N` next to percentile if effective-N < 100, and clicking reveals raw sample distribution by origin.

Josh: I'll make a tracking ticket and attach Maria's repro and Kevin's counts. For immediate ops: add runbook note — "When route p99 and endpoint p99 disagree, check sample_origin counts and effective N before paging SRE." I'll tag eng-platform and oncall.

Maria: thanks all — tagging @eng-platform for visibility. :eyes:

Liz: created a tiny mock PR for the tooltip + badge text, PTAL: https://git.internal/redwood/console/pull/5421 :thumbsup:

Kevin: I'll drop a short metric to surface `percentile_effective_n` in the next infra deploy so the console can consume it.

Josh: good plan. I'll update the dashboard doc with the new FAQ entry and link the PR. closing the loop here. :+1:
